figures.title: Dural sinuses and deep veins
figures.alt: Dural sinuses and deep veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: Sagittal and frontal MR venography projections retain seven numbered labels. The key follows the authors’ identifications.

figures.title: Basal veins
figures.alt: Basal veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: The red arrow identifies the basal veins on the supplied axial MRV panel. The article caption also mentions a sagittal plane, which is absent from this figure.

figures.title: Septal, thalamostriate and internal cerebral veins
figures.alt: Septal, thalamostriate and internal cerebral veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: The sagittal MRV view and circular axial inset retain the authors’ coloured arrows. The key follows the source caption.

figures.title: Superficial cortical veins · DSA
figures.alt: Lateral digital subtraction angiography with three original coloured arrows identifying the superficial middle cerebral, Trolard and Labbé veins.
figures.caption: The red arrow identifies the superficial middle cerebral vein, green identifies the superior anastomotic vein of Trolard, and blue identifies the inferior anastomotic vein of Labbé. This published DSA projection has no specified patient side.

figures.title: Right lateral-sinus filling defect · MRV
figures.alt: Right lateral-sinus filling defect · MRV in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: Panels a and b are maximum-intensity projections. Panels c and d are selected source-slice images. The authors identify interruption of the proximal right lateral sinus and a filling defect suggesting thrombus. These panels provide selected views of the finding.

figures.title: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis · CT
figures.alt: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis · CT in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: Panel a shows source-described superior sagittal sinus hyperdensity on nonenhanced CT. Panel b shows the empty delta sign on contrast-enhanced CT. The publication supplies selected sections, with no complete thrombus measurement or named venography protocol.

figures.title: Deep venous thrombosis with haemorrhagic infarction · MRI
figures.alt: Deep venous thrombosis with haemorrhagic infarction · MRI in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: The authors describe a 27-year-old woman with deep venous thrombosis. Panel A shows absent flow signal in the internal cerebral veins (arrow) and vein of Galen. Panel B shows haemorrhagic venous infarction in the left caudate head and thalamus on susceptibility-weighted MRI. The source explicitly states that the straight sinus is not demonstrated.
labels: MR venogram with one orange arrow

figures.title: Jugular bulb landmarks · CBCT
figures.alt: Jugular bulb landmarks · CBCT in the original coronal image panels.
figures.caption: White outline marks the bulb. SUP, INF, LAT and MED are visible around it. Patient laterality is unspecified.

figures.title: Jugular bulb variants · CBCT
figures.alt: Jugular bulb variants · CBCT in the original coronal image panels.
figures.caption: The authors compare five jugular bulb variants on coronal cone-beam CT. In panel D, the dotted line marks the floor of the internal acoustic canal. These images illustrate anatomy and variants.

figures.title: Temporal horn enlargement with venous thrombosis
figures.alt: Four original panels. Left column axial FLAIR MRI. Right column nonenhanced axial CT from a different patient.
figures.caption: Panels A and B are FLAIR MRI from one patient with deep oedema and enlargement of both temporal horns. Panels C and D are nonenhanced CT from a different patient with a large left hemispheric haemorrhage and widening of the opposite temporal horn. The source provides selected sections.
labels: FLAIR MRI · bilateral temporal horn enlargement
Nonenhanced CT · left hemispheric haemorrhage and contralateral temporal horn widening
